key_insight: AI applied to routine echocardiography can detect an adverse epicardial fat phenotype that tracks with cardiometabolic dysfunction better than standard echo measures.
clinical_relevance: This could make risk stratification for cardiometabolic disease more scalable by using imaging already common in clinical care, though it is not yet a diagnostic or treatment tool.
method: Trained a video-based deep learning model (PanAdipo) on 1.1M echo videos from 28,797 studies.
Validated performance across multiple cohorts, including health-system, emergency department, MIMIC-IV, and MESA datasets.
Compared AI scores with CT-derived body composition, biomarkers, and incident metabolic outcomes.
evidence_signal: PanAdipo achieved AUROC 0.91 for prominent epicardial adipose tissue in held-out testing and showed strongest correlation with CT epicardial fat (Spearman rho=0.75), with associations to insulin resistance, triglycerides, and new metabolic disease.
watch_item: The model requires external validation and careful implementation because performance may vary by scanner, site, and patient population, and it identifies risk rather than proving causality.
paper_title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies an Adverse Epicardial Adiposity Phenotype Associated with Cardiometabolic Dysfunction
